title: Composite Panel Delamination — Injection Repair Practice
abstract: General injection repair practice for delamination in secondary composite panels, giving the tap test and ultrasonic mapping method, the injection sequence and the limits beyond which a scarf repair is required.

sections.purpose: To give the general practice for repairing delamination in secondary composite panels by resin injection, and the limits beyond which the panel needs a scarf repair or replacement.
sections.damage_assessment: Delamination in a secondary panel is usually caused by an edge impact or by water ingress at a fastener. Map the extent by tap test first and then confirm with an ultrasonic scan, because the tap test finds the boundary quickly but under-reads a deep delamination between the inner plies. Record the mapped area, the depth of the affected interface and the distance to the nearest edge and fastener. Damage that reaches a free edge, that involves more than three interfaces, or that lies within a load-introduction area is outside this scheme and needs a scarf repair. Dry the panel before any assessment is finalised; a wet delamination reads larger on the ultrasonic scan than it is.
sections.repair_procedure: Mark the mapped boundary on the panel with a non-permanent marker. Dry the area with the heat blanket at the temperature and duration in the table and record the cycle. Drill the injection holes at the positions on the drawing, sized to the drill in the tooling list, taking care not to break through the far face. CAUTION applies at this step and is stated on the drawing. Clean the holes with dry filtered air. Mix the injection resin to the ratio on the container and record the mix time. Inject from the lowest hole and work upwards, watching for resin at the next hole before moving to it. Continue until resin appears at every hole in the group. Apply the vacuum bag and the heat blanket and run the cure cycle in the table. Record the cure cycle from the thermocouple trace. Remove the bag and fill the injection holes with the filler compound. Where the panel edge has been opened, install the splice plate D5170003839797 or the stiffener EL25483-60 as the drawing requires, using rivets AGS611113-6C. Sand the repaired surface flush and re-apply the paint scheme.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an ultrasonic scan of the repaired area at completion and keep the trace as the baseline. Repeat the ultrasonic scan at the next heavy check and thereafter at every second heavy check. A repaired area that shows any growth beyond the original boundary must be referred for a scarf repair; a second injection at the same location is not permitted.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Mapped delamination up to 4 500 square millimetres, involving no more than three interfaces, no closer than 30 mm to a free edge and not within a load-introduction area. Not applicable to primary structure.

type_data.fastener_pattern: No new fasteners within the injected area. Where an edge splice is installed, one row of 18 solid rivets at 20 mm pitch with 15 mm edge distance.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit is attached provided the repeat ultrasonic scan shows no growth. Growth beyond the original mapped boundary requires a scarf repair and this scheme may not be applied a second time at the same location.
